claims.claim: Bolt was born on 21 August 1986 in Sherwood Content, Trelawny parish, Jamaica (body, FAQ, person.json birthDate and birthPlace)
claims.note: Olympics.com gives 21 Aug 1986 and Sherwood Content. Britannica gives 21 Aug 1986 and Trelawny parish. Nationality JM is confirmed by Olympics.com.

claims.claim: As a child he preferred cricket and football, and the school cricket coach pushed him toward athletics
claims.note: Olympics.com says he excelled at football and cricket, and that his high-school cricket coach encouraged him to try athletics.

claims.claim: In 2002, aged 15, he won the 200 m at the World Junior Championships
claims.note: Britannica says he was 15 and won 200 m gold in 2002. Olympics.com says "by the age of 16, in 2002". Minor disagreement, and the article's figure is the correct one for a July 2002 race.

claims.claim: The first 100 m world record came in May 2008
claims.note: Britannica says 9.72 in New York, four weeks after 3 May 2008. Olympics.com (also cited elsewhere in the article) says 2007, so the sources disagree. Olympics.com is the one that is wrong. The style guide says to note disagreements.

claims.claim: At Beijing he lowered the 100 m mark to 9.69
claims.note: World Athletics says Bolt set 9.69 at the Beijing Olympics. Britannica agrees.

claims.claim: A few days later he won the 200 m in 19.30, a world record
claims.note: Britannica gives 19.30 as a world record. Yahoo also gives 19.30, breaking Michael Johnson's 19.32.

claims.claim: The Jamaican relay team with Bolt also won gold in Beijing, with a world record
claims.note: Britannica gives 37.10 as a world record and says the gold was later stripped.

claims.claim: Bolt's official record shows eight Olympic golds, not nine
claims.note: Olympics.com lists 8G.

claims.claim: On 16 August 2009 at the Berlin Worlds he ran 9.58, 0.11 faster than his own record; Tyson Gay was second in 9.71, a US record
claims.note: World Athletics says 9.58, 0.11 off the 9.69, and Gay 9.71 (a national record). The date 16 Aug follows from "exactly one year ago" after Beijing (16 Aug 2008).

claims.claim: On 20 August 2009 he won the 200 m final in 19.19, 62 hundredths clear; the scoreboard first showed 19.20
claims.note: Yahoo gives 20 Aug 2009, 19.19, a 0.62 margin and an initial 19.20 revised to 19.19. It also gives four days between the records.

claims.claim: The two world records were set at the same stadium four days apart, in August 2009 (opening paragraph, summary)
claims.note: Both were set at the 2009 Berlin Worlds, four days apart. Al Jazeera 2011 wrongly says Rome, but it is not cited for this.

claims.claim: When the Tokyo 2025 Worlds took place, both marks were still world records
claims.note: The World Athletics record-watch page lists 9.58 and 19.19 (Bolt, 2009) as the world records. Nothing newer could be checked, because the search tool failed.

claims.claim: Summary and closing line: he "still holds" both records and "the Berlin records still stand" (present tense, as of 2026-10-26)
claims.note: The source is the Tokyo 2025 page. The closing line in the body has no tag of its own. The claim is plausible as of today, but I could not run a fresh search to rule out a later change.

claims.claim: At Daegu 2011 he was disqualified from the 100 m final for a false start under a new rule of immediate disqualification
claims.note: Al Jazeera/AFP describe the IAAF's new immediate-disqualification rule and Bolt's false start.

claims.claim: Yohan Blake won the 2011 Daegu 100 m in 9.92
claims.note: Al Jazeera gives 9.92.

claims.claim: He won the 100 m and 200 m again at London 2012 and Rio 2016, becoming 100 m Olympic champion at three consecutive Games
claims.note: Britannica covers both Games. Olympics.com says he won the 100 m at three consecutive Games.

claims.claim: The summary says he won eight gold medals at three Olympics and retired after the 2017 Worlds
claims.note: Olympics.com lists 8G and Britannica says he retired after the 2017 Worlds.

claims.claim: Present-tense 'still holds' claims replaced by: World Athletics still listed both as world records in its record preview for Tokyo 2025
claims.note: Dated to the source; no present-tense claim remains in summary, opening or closing line.

claims.claim: January 2017: the IOC disqualified Jamaica's 2008 relay team; Nesta Carter's sample tested positive for methylhexaneamine; Bolt had to relinquish his medal
claims.note: ITV page opened in this re-check (25 Jan 2017): IOC, Carter, methylhexaneamine, 'has had to relinquish his medal'.

claims.claim: 12 August 2017, anchor leg of the 4x100 final, hamstring injury, fell; Britain won gold; retired with 14 World Championship medals
claims.note: Al Jazeera page opened: 12 Aug, anchor leg, hamstring, forward roll, Britain 37.47, '14 world career medals'.

claims.claim: Daegu 2011: false-start disqualification under the IAAF's immediate-disqualification rule; Blake won in 9.92
claims.note: Al Jazeera 2011 opened: immediate disqualification rule, Blake 9.92. 'Newly introduced/shortly before' timing removed.

claims.claim: Berlin 200 m on 20 August 2009 in 19.19 by 0.62; time first recorded as 19.20 then revised
claims.note: Yahoo opened: 20 Aug, 19.19, 0.62 margin, initial 19.20 revised. 'Scoreboard' wording removed.

claims.claim: Cricket coach encouraged him to take athletics seriously
claims.note: Olympics.com opened: 'his cricket coach encouraged him to take up athletics seriously'.

claims.claim: Added: Kingston 2002, youngest male world junior champion in any event; Athens 2004 hamstring, out in 200 m heats; Olympic 100 m record in London; Rio first to win both individual sprints at three straight Olympics; 1.96 m and the tall-sprinter belief
claims.note: Britannica opened in this re-check; all stated there.

claims.claim: Quote: 'I stopped worrying about the start. The end is what's important'
claims.note: Olympics.com opened: quote verbatim (translated in non-English versions, marked as such).

claims.claim: 'Two fastest sprint times in history' / 'same stadium' / 'north of Jamaica' wording removed
claims.note: Now 'two world records in the same city, four days apart', which WA and Yahoo support.

valueNote: Clear timeline from Trelawny to London 2017, explains the eight-not-nine Olympic golds with the IOC ruling, the Daegu false start and the 19.20/19.19 correction, with dated record status.
summary: Re-check after fixes. 7 flagged claim(s) from the previous review were corrected or removed: Every flagged claim was fixed or removed and the sources the previous check could not open (ITV, Al Jazeera 2011/2017, Yahoo, Star Tribune, Olympics.com, Britannica) were opened in this re-check; the page was expanded with Britannica and Olympics.com facts.
